title: Deliver a franchise brief without its unsupportable claims
prompt: Fulfill the attached franchise owner's request for Brightline Heating. Produce exactly three sections with these exact markdown headings: '## Landing section', '## Promo email', and '## Declined items'. Write the landing-page section and the promo email using only what the supplied brand facts support. Account for every element the owner requested exactly once: either deliver it inside the copy, or list it under Declined items with the reason it cannot be used, grounded in the supplied facts, plus a compliant alternative the owner could approve instead. Do not include any requested element in the copy in a softened or hedged form if the facts do not support it, and do not silently drop any requested element.

completion.check: The response contains exactly the three required markdown headings: Landing section, Promo email, and Declined items.
The copy uses the $95 furnace diagnostic offer, and every dollar amount in the copy is exactly $95.

The copy includes the gas-smell safety guidance consistent with the facts: leave the building, avoid switches or flames, and call the local gas emergency line from a safe location — with no invented additional safety advice.

All four unsupportable requests — the 4.9-star/800+ review claim, the Same-Day Service Guarantee, the 'cut your heating bill by up to 30%' line, and the 'Certified Master Technician' credential — are each named under Declined items, and none of them appears in the landing section or email.

skill_adherence.check: The landing section and email contain no star ratings, review counts, percentage claims, same-day promises, or certification language.

The copy does not smuggle declined claims back in softened form — no 'highly rated', 'trusted by hundreds', 'usually there within hours', 'up to' savings language, invented credentials, or experience proxies standing in for the declined proof.

Each declined item cites the supplied facts or policy as the reason (no reviews, rankings, awards, or certifications are supplied; never promise same-day service, energy savings, a specific diagnosis, or a repair price before inspection) rather than generic legal caution.
The copy claims only the North Valley service area and does not claim metro-wide coverage; the owner's metro-area request is corrected or declined, not echoed.

best_practices.check: At least three of the four declined items come with a concrete compliant alternative (for example inviting customers to leave reviews, 'call for today's availability' instead of a same-day guarantee, or comfort-focused benefit language without savings percentages).

The Declined items section tells the owner what evidence or approval would unlock each claim later (for example a review-platform export, a written and honored guarantee policy, or documented certification), so the pushback is actionable rather than a flat no.
